newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ATHLETICS-NDETI STEPS INTO OLDER BROTHER'S SHOES. [CORRECTED 02:41 GMT 24/4]
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-NDETI STEPS INTO OLDER BROTHER'S SHOES. [CORRECTED 02:41 GMT 24/4]

text.p: Belgrade marathon champion Josephat Ndeti has literally stepped into the shoes of three times Boston winner and elder brother Cosmas.
Eight years ago, Josephat started running in shoes given to him by Cosmas, two years his senior.
"It started me running," he said. "I simply followed his example, we are great friends."
The brothers still train together although Josephat, now 23, is now very much his own man.
Despite his comparative youth, he owns and runs three livestock farms, supervising three farmhands.
He has two sons, aged six and three, and also assists his wife with an ice cream business.
Despite these responsibilities, Ndeti went off the rails three years ago after a successful junior career.
"I was drinking and smoking, doing bad things, mixing with bad people," Ndeti said.
"I was still running, but not very well. Then I realised I was wasting my life. I turned to the Bible and I was saved."
"Saved" is a term which frequently peppers Ndeti's conversation.
When asked to elaborate, Ndeti cites world heavyweight champion Evander Holyfield.
"That man was saved, that's how he beat Mike Tyson," he said.
"I decided to be saved also. That's why I knew I would win here."
Despite his outward confidence, Ndeti had to fight hard to win on a sultry day when temperatures rose to 21 degrees Celsius.
Ndeti clocked two hours 13 minutes 38 seconds, just seven seconds ahead of compatriot Reuben Chebutich who as making his marathon debut.
Onesmus Mutisya. a cousin of the Ndeti's, was third in 2:12.02.

Ndeti has never raced in one of the major marathons in the United States, such as Boston or New York (corrects to make clear that Honolulu is in the United States). The closest he has come is the Honolulu marathon in 1993 when he finished third behind his brother's second.
This year he plans to run the Berlin marathon in the northern autumn on the course where his compatriot Sammy Lelei set the world's second fastest time in 1995.
The Berlin organisers are certain they have got a world record course. And Ndeti is certain he can run a world record.
"I can to 2:06, even 2:05 if necessary," he said.
